context:
Goal: an Opus ask lets in only the Opus you meant.
Problem (rule): your ruling on item 601 a (12:54 CST Nov 12) says "an Opus ask with no length lasts until the session ends or `opus off`". At 13:26 CST today you typed "send a blind opus agent to understand what are all the roles...", meaning one agent. The hook stored a 2-hour Opus grant for every role in that session (written 19:26:53Z, ends 21:26:49Z, role null; the file sits in the cloud container, so no cloud session can revoke it), and at 14:13 CST you said "opus override for this session? what are you talking about". At 14:18 CST, relayed by the retrospective, you said of the options: "oh my version is too generous and yours is too tight there's an optimal middle ground though if you thinka bout it". Option d is the retrospective's middle ground, not your words; it needs your word because it replaces 601 a.
Based on (ruling): item 601 a, record 618b84ece; your rule that a grant covers the act it names, never a variant.
Based on (read): the retrospective's reading of the grant file and hooks/local_time.py; triage has not read either. A draft, #2928 (head 96416a2d6), already builds 601 a.
Departs from: main — an Opus ask with no length lasts until the session ends; b, c and d shorten it.
Meanwhile: step opus-ask-grants-one-spawn is held with no lane; #2928 is unaffected.

options.label: Keep 601 a: a plain Opus ask lasts until the session ends or `opus off`
options.lose: You called this too generous: a one-agent ask can still open Opus for every role until the session ends.

options.gain: A grant covers exactly one agent.
options.label: A plain Opus ask grants the one spawn it names
options.lose: You called this too tight: a retry or resume of that agent, or a second agent for the same ask, needs a second ask. Reverses 601 a.

options.gain: A long session cannot carry it far.
options.label: A plain Opus ask ends at your next typed message
options.lose: Reverses 601 a; it is the option you did not pick on 601 (its option b), and agents that run across your messages lose Opus mid-task.

options.gain: Every agent spawned for that ask, in the turn you typed it, plus any resume or retry of those same agents by name, may run Opus; if the ask names a role ("opus reviewers"), only that role. The grant ends when those agents end. `opus <time>` keeps its timed form; `opus off` ends any grant. The work you asked for gets Opus through retries; nothing else in the session does.
options.label: A plain Opus ask grants Opus to the task it names, not to a clock and not to one spawn (Recommended)
options.lose: Reverses 601 a. The hook must tie a grant to a turn and its agents, which is more code than a clock.

owner: coordinator (session_013NEJL1gw6EdrSyvHkTUEx6), from the retrospective; posted by triage (session_013NEJKzCzoWhfP8FMCPtQU6)
reply: Filed: ruling own-761-d-task-scoped-opus (roadmap c5bd54199). A plain Opus ask grants Opus to the agents spawned for it, plus resumes and retries of those agents by name; role-scoped if the ask names a role; it ends when those agents end. `opus <time>` stays timed; `opus off` ends any grant. This rewrites the Opus half of 601 a. Step opus-ask-grants-one-spawn is unblocked and stacks on #2928. Your word came by chat ("agreed", 14:21 CST, relayed by the retrospective), so no page answer exists.
short: Opus ask: task-scoped, one spawn, or session?
title: How long should a plain Opus ask last: the task it names, one spawn, or until the session ends?
why: The step that fixes the 2-hour grant reverses your recorded ruling 601 a, and the step's reading is the retrospective's, not your words.
